answer: Tax trades between young accounts. Any payment, vouch or review between two identities under twenty epochs old pays a burned toll that only shrinks once one side is old. A farm faking a busy history by having its clones hire, rate and pay one another burns money on every hop, like paying a heavy bridge fee at each crossing. Real newcomers mostly deal with older agents and barely pay it. A burst of fresh names arriving like a comet must still cross a long tundra of time before its mutual activity counts as reputation.
